# Finding the Antiderivative of x³ sin(x)

I'll use **integration by parts** repeatedly (or the tabular/DI method).

## Setup

$$\int x^3 \sin(x)\, dx$$

## Step-by-step Integration by Parts

**First application:** Let $u = x^3$, $dv = \sin(x)\,dx$

$$\int x^3 \sin(x)\, dx = -x^3\cos(x) + \int 3x^2 \cos(x)\, dx$$

**Second application:** Let $u = 3x^2$, $dv = \cos(x)\,dx$

$$\int 3x^2 \cos(x)\, dx = 3x^2\sin(x) - \int 6x \sin(x)\, dx$$

**Third application:** Let $u = 6x$, $dv = \sin(x)\,dx$

$$\int 6x \sin(x)\, dx = -6x\cos(x) + \int 6\cos(x)\, dx = -6x\cos(x) + 6\sin(x)$$

## Combining Results

$$\int x^3 \sin(x)\, dx = -x^3\cos(x) + 3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification (by differentiation)

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[-x^3\cos(x) + 3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x)\right]$$

$$= \underbrace{(-3x^2\cos(x) + x^3\sin(x))}_{\text{from } -x^3\cos(x)} + \underbrace{(6x\sin(x) + 3x^2\cos(x))}_{\text{from } 3x^2\sin(x)} + \underbrace{(6\cos(x) - 6x\sin(x))}_{\text{from } 6x\cos(x)} + \underbrace{(-6\cos(x))}_{\text{from } -6\sin(x)}$$

All intermediate terms cancel, leaving $x^3\sin(x)$ ✓

<answer>-x**3*cos(x) + 3*x**2*sin(x) + 6*x*cos(x) - 6*sin(x) + C</answer>
